page: Microsoft Azure FX12-6mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 3 dedicated physical cores and 2 threads per core, yielding 6 vCPUs. It is equipped with 252.0 GB of RAM, translating to 42.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. There are no GPUs bundled with this server type.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves a top-tier rating in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform strongly, ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 518.17 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds are 51.24 GB/sec and 36.64 GB/sec, respectively. In LLM inference, the server demonstrates strong performance for text generation with a small 135M model, but exhibits weaker performance on larger models, such as the 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX12-6mds_v2 offers a highly dense memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a specialized resource for memory-bound applications rather than general-purpose compute. The inclusion of a 945 GB local NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space without requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, text processing pipelines, single-threaded data compression tasks, and lightweight language model inference.
